cues.en: Imagine
cues.zh: 想象一下

cues.en: a world in which one of the things owned by a corporation was the song Happy Birthday.
cues.zh: 这样一个世界：一家公司拥有的东西之一，竟然是《生日快乐》这首歌。

cues.en: In fact, an AOL Time Warner subsidiary holds the copyright.
cues.zh: 事实上，一家 AOL Time Warner 旗下的子公司持有这首歌的版权。

cues.en: In the past, it has demanded over $10,000
cues.zh: 过去，它曾要求支付超过 1 万美元

cues.en: to allow you to hear anyone sing this popular song in a film.
cues.zh: 才允许你在电影里听到任何人唱这首流行歌曲。

cues.en: We didn't pay.
cues.zh: 我们没付钱。

cues.en: We preferred to use the money to fly our crew to Boston and Los Angeles to bring you the following story. Five,
cues.zh: 我们宁愿用这笔钱把摄制组送到波士顿和洛杉矶，为你带来下面这个故事。五，

cues.en: four, three, two, one. Off into space.
cues.zh: 四、三、二、一。发射升空。

cues.en: Man, that takes real teamwork.
cues.zh: 天哪，这真需要团队合作。

cues.en: And here's a team of junior spacemen with an out of this world breakfast. Comparing
cues.zh: 这是一队小宇航员，正享用着美味绝伦的早餐。将

cues.en: the marketing of yesteryear to the marketing of today is like comparing a BB gun to a smart bomb. It's
cues.zh: 过去的营销与今天的营销相比，简直就像拿BB弹气枪去比智能炸弹。它

cues.en: not the same as when I was a kid or even when the people who are young adults today were kids.
cues.zh: 和我小时候，甚至和现在的年轻人小时候，都完全不同了。

cues.en: It's much more sophisticated and it's much more pervasive.
cues.zh: 现在的营销要成熟得多，也更加无孔不入。

cues.en: It's not that
cues.zh: 并不是说

cues.en: products
cues.zh: 产品

cues.en: themselves
cues.zh: 本身

cues.en: are bad or good.
cues.zh: 有好坏之分。

cues.en: It's the notion
cues.zh: 这是指

cues.en: of manipulating
cues.zh: 诱导

cues.en: children into buying products.
cues.zh: 孩子购买产品。

cues.en: Western International Media, Century City, and Liberman Research Worldwide conducted a study on nagging.
cues.zh: Western International Media、Century City 和 Liberman Research Worldwide 联合开展了一项关于孩子纠缠父母的研究。

cues.en: We asked parents to keep a diary for three weeks and to record every time. You could imagine, every time their child
cues.zh: 我们请家长记三周日记，每次都记录下来。你们可以想象，每当他们的孩子

cues.en: nagged them for a product,
cues.zh: 缠着他们要买某种产品时，

cues.en: we asked them to record when,
cues.zh: 我们都会请他们记下时间、

cues.en: where, and why.
cues.zh: 地点和原因。

cues.en: Study was not to help parents cope with nagging.
cues.zh: 这项研究并不是为了帮助家长应对孩子的纠缠。

cues.en: It was to help corporations
cues.zh: 最初的目的是帮助企业

cues.en: help children nag for their products more effectively.
cues.zh: 帮助孩子们更有效地缠着父母买他们的产品。

cues.en: Anywhere from twenty percent to 40% of purchases would not have occurred unless the child had nagged their parents.
cues.zh: 除非孩子缠着父母，否则有20%到40%的购买行为根本不会发生。

cues.en: That is we found, for example,
cues.zh: 我们发现，例如，

cues.en: a quarter of all visits to theme parks
cues.zh: 在所有主题公园的游玩中，有四分之一

cues.en: wouldn't have occurred unless a child nagged their parents.
cues.zh: 除非孩子缠着父母，否则根本不会发生。

cues.en: Four out of 10 visits to places like Chuck E. Cheese would not have occurred.
cues.zh: 去Chuck E. Cheese这类地方的游玩中，十次里有四次本来不会发生。

cues.en: And any parent would understand that, you know, when I think of Chuck E. Cheese, oh my goodness, it's noise.
cues.zh: 任何家长都能理解，你知道，我一想到 Chuck E. Cheese，天哪，简直吵翻了。

cues.en: And there's so many kids, why would I want to spend two hours there? But if the child nags enough, you're going to go. We saw the same thing with movies,
cues.zh: 孩子又那么多，我干吗要在那儿待两个小时？可孩子缠得够久，你最后还是会去。电影也是一样，

cues.en: with home video, with fast food.
cues.zh: 家庭录像也是，快餐也是。

cues.en: We do have to break through this barrier where they do tell us or they say they don't like it when their kids nag. Well that's just a general attitude that they possess.
cues.zh: 我们确实得打破这种障碍：他们会告诉我们，或者说他们不喜欢孩子缠着要东西。其实这只是他们普遍的一种态度。

cues.en: It doesn't mean that they necessarily
cues.zh: 这并不意味着他们一定会

cues.en: act upon it 100% of the time.
cues.zh: 百分之百付诸行动。

cues.en: You can manipulate
cues.zh: 你可以操纵

cues.en: consumers
cues.zh: 消费者，

cues.en: into
cues.zh: 让他们

cues.en: wanting and therefore buying your products.
cues.zh: 产生渴望，进而购买你的产品。

cues.en: It's a game.
cues.zh: 这就是一场博弈。

cues.en: Children are not little adults.
cues.zh: 儿童并不是缩小版的成人。

cues.en: Their minds aren't developed.
cues.zh: 他们的心智尚未成熟。

cues.en: And what's happening is that marketers are playing to their developmental
cues.zh: 而营销人员正在利用他们发育中的

cues.en: vulnerabilities.
cues.zh: 弱点。

cues.en: The advertising that children are exposed to today
cues.zh: 如今儿童所接触的广告

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: honed by psychologists,
cues.zh: 经过心理学家精心打磨的，

cues.en: it's enhanced by media technology that nobody ever thought was possible. The more insight you have about the consumer,
cues.zh: 并由前所未见的媒体技术赋能。你对消费者了解越深，

cues.en: the more creative you'll be in your communication strategies.
cues.zh: 你的传播策略就越有创意。

cues.en: If that takes a psychologist,
cues.zh: 如果这需要心理学家，

cues.en: yeah, we want one of those on staff.
cues.zh: 那我们想请一位加入团队。

cues.en: I'm not saying that it's wrong to make things for children.
cues.zh: 我不是说给孩子做东西就不对。

cues.en: I also think it's important to distinguish between psychologists who work on products for children, toy
cues.zh: 我也觉得，区分为儿童产品工作的心理学家和玩具公司很重要。

cues.en: corporations
cues.zh: 公司

cues.en: make toys that are developmentally appropriate.
cues.zh: 会制作适合儿童发展阶段的玩具。

cues.en: I think that's great. That's different from selling the toys directly to the children.
cues.zh: 我觉得这很好。这和直接把玩具卖给孩子是两回事。

cues.en: Initiative is huge. I think in The US we place about $12,000,000,000
cues.zh: 主动性很重要。我觉得在美国，我们投入了大约120亿美元

cues.en: of media time.
cues.zh: 的媒体时间。

cues.en: So we'll put it on TV, we'll put it in print, we'll put it out in outdoor, we'll buy radio time. So we're the biggest buyers
cues.zh: 所以我们会投电视、投平面、投户外，还会买广播时段。我们是大买家

cues.en: of advertising time and space in The US and in The world.
cues.zh: 在美国乃至全球购买广告时间和版面的最大买家。

cues.en: One family cannot combat
cues.zh: 一个家庭无法对抗

cues.en: an industry that spends $12,000,000,000
cues.zh: 一个每年花费120亿美元

cues.en: a year trying to get their children. They can't do it.
cues.zh: 试图影响他们孩子的行业。他们做不到。

cues.en: They are tomorrow's adult consumers, so start talking with them now,
cues.zh: 他们是明天的成年消费者，所以现在就和他们对话，

cues.en: build that relationship when they're younger, and you've got them as an adult.
cues.zh: 在他们还小的时候建立那种关系，等他们成年就是你的客户了。

cues.en: Somebody asked me, Lucy, is that ethical?
cues.zh: 有人问我：“Lucy，这样合乎伦理吗？”

cues.en: You're essentially manipulating these children.
cues.zh: “你们其实是在操纵这些孩子。”

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: yeah, is it ethical? I don't know. But our our role at initiative is to move products. And if we know you move products with a certain creative execution
cues.zh: 是啊，这合乎伦理吗？我不知道。但我们在 Initiative 的职责就是卖出产品。如果我们知道，把某个创意广告放在某类媒体渠道上就能卖出产品，

cues.en: placed in a certain type of media vehicle, then we've done our job.
cues.zh: 那我们就算完成任务了。

cues.en: Every
cues.zh: 每个

cues.en: institution provides
cues.zh: 机构都会给

cues.en: the people who are members of it
cues.zh: 其中的成员

cues.en: with a social role to occupy.
cues.zh: 安排一种社会角色。

cues.en: And typically,
cues.zh: 通常，

cues.en: institutions that are vibrant and and have a lot of power
cues.zh: 那些充满活力、拥有很大权力的机构

cues.en: will
cues.zh: 会

cues.en: specify that role in in some sense as as a list of virtues. It's true for churches, for schools, for for any institution that that has power over over people and and shapes them. One nation. The corporation, likewise, it provides us with a list of virtues, a kind of social role, which is the good consumer.
cues.zh: 在某种意义上，把这种角色列成一系列美德。教会、学校都是如此，任何掌控他人、塑造他人的机构也都是如此。国家如此，公司也一样。它会给我们列出一系列美德，赋予我们一种社会角色：做一个好消费者。

cues.en: Like the waters of a mighty ocean, people also represent a tremendous force,
cues.zh: 就像汪洋大海的波涛一样，大众也代表着一股巨大的力量，

cues.en: the understanding of which is of greatest importance to the American way of life. This
cues.zh: 理解这股力量对美国的生活方式至关重要。这种

cues.en: force is known as consumer power.
cues.zh: 力量被称为消费者的力量。

cues.en: The goal for the corporations is to maximize profit and market share,
cues.zh: 大企业的目标是实现利润和市场份额的最大化，

cues.en: and they also have a goal for their target, namely the population.
cues.zh: 而他们对自己的目标受众，也就是大众，也同样有着明确的目标。

cues.en: They have to be turned into
cues.zh: 那就是必须把他们变成

cues.en: completely
cues.zh: 彻底

cues.en: mindless consumers
cues.zh: 盲目的消费者，

cues.en: of goods that they do not want.
cues.zh: 去消费他们根本不需要的商品。

cues.en: You have to
cues.zh: 你得

cues.en: develop what are called created wants. So you have to create wants.
cues.zh: 去开发所谓的“制造需求”，也就是说你得创造需求。

cues.en: You have to impose on people what's called a philosophy of futility.
cues.zh: 你得向人们灌输一种所谓的“无用哲学”。

cues.en: You have to focus them on insignificant
cues.zh: 你得让他们把注意力集中在无足轻重的

cues.en: things of life, like fashionable consumption.
cues.zh: 生活琐事上，比如时尚消费。

cues.en: I'm
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: just basically quoting business literature,
cues.zh: 基本上就是在引用商业文献，

cues.en: and it makes perfect sense. The ideal is to have individuals who are totally dissociated from one another,
cues.zh: 而且这完全说得通。理想状态就是让个体彼此完全隔绝，

cues.en: whose conception of themselves,
cues.zh: 他们对自我的认知、

cues.en: sense of value,
cues.zh: 价值感，

cues.en: is just how many created wants can I satisfy?
cues.zh: 仅仅取决于我能满足多少被制造出来的需求？

cues.en: These
cues.zh: 这些

cues.en: people are customers
cues.zh: 人是客户

cues.en: because they are willing to trade money for widgets.
cues.zh: 因为他们愿意用钱换小部件。

cues.en: And all the customers take their widgets home to all parts of the country.
cues.zh: 所有客户都把买到的小部件带回家，带到全国各地。

cues.en: Look at all that money the widget builder has taken in from the sale of his widgets.
cues.zh: 看看这个小部件制造商从卖小部件中赚了多少钱。

cues.en: We have huge industries. Public relations industry is a monstrous industry.
cues.zh: 我们还有庞大的产业。公关产业就是个巨型产业。

cues.en: Advertising and so on is...
cues.zh: 广告之类的……

cues.en: Which are designed from infancy
cues.zh: 它们从人一出生就开始设计

cues.en: to try to
cues.zh: 试图

cues.en: mold people into this desired pattern.
cues.zh: 把人塑造成期望的模样。

cues.en: We saw Tiger Woods on TV with a hat with a Nike logo on it, and we figured, you know, he probably gets, like, millions of dollars just to wear the hat on the press conference. And therefore, we figured we can do that for someone else and hopefully get money in terms so we can go to school.
cues.zh: 我们在电视上看到老虎伍兹戴着一顶印有耐克标志的帽子，就觉得他大概只要在新闻发布会上戴着这顶帽子，就能拿到几百万美元。所以我们想，或许也能找别人做这件事，希望能赚到钱，这样我们就能上大学了。

cues.en: And that's how we came up with being corporately sponsored.
cues.zh: 这就是我们想到让企业赞助我们的由来。

cues.en: We made our sponsor announcement on today's show on June 18. We're thrilled to be sponsored by First USA. We're thrilled to be working with First USA as our corporate sponsor, and they're covering our college tuition to found First USA as our sponsor, and we're proud to be working with them. Our sponsor is First USA, so we are really thrilled
cues.zh: 我们在今天的节目中，于6月18日宣布了赞助商。我们很高兴能得到第一美国银行的赞助，也很高兴能与第一美国银行合作，由他们承担我们的大学学费。第一美国银行是我们的赞助商，我们很荣幸能与他们合作。我们的赞助商是第一美国银行，所以我们非常高兴

cues.en: to announce,
cues.zh: 地宣布，

cues.en: First USA as our sponsor. We're thrilled to be working with First USA. And so we give First USA a good name in the media and include them in our news stories. And then through there, they get as much advertising as we can give them. They'll be conforming not to the wishes of demanding parents,
cues.zh: 第一美国银行成为我们的赞助商。我们很高兴能与第一美国银行合作。因此，我们会在媒体上为第一美国银行树立良好形象，也会在新闻报道中提到他们。我们会尽可能让他们获得更多广告曝光。他们会顺着要求多多的家长们的意思，

cues.en: but to the wishes of an image conscious corporation.
cues.zh: 而是顺应一家注重形象的公司的意愿。

cues.en: They're not just out there for the money and they're just... I mean, they wanna work with us and be our friends and then... And let us help them, help us, and vice versa. We became walking billboards to pay for our college tuition. Get out of way. Cool site of the day picked us as cool site, and Yahoo picked us, and we were in USA Today. When we did our photo shoot for People Magazine,
cues.zh: 他们不只是为了钱，他们只是……我是说，他们想和我们合作，做我们的朋友，然后……让我们互帮互助。为了交大学学费，我们成了行走的广告牌。闪开。“今日酷站”把我们选为酷站，Yahoo 也选了我们，我们还上了《今日美国》。在给《人物》杂志拍宣传照时，

cues.en: this is where we stood,
cues.zh: 我们就是站在这里，

cues.en: up on top.
cues.zh: 就站在这上面。

cues.en: We stood up here and we smiled. We smiled and took the picture.
cues.zh: 我们站在这里，微笑着。我们微笑着拍了照。

cues.en: Our parents had war stories and stuff to tell us. We
cues.zh: 我们的父母有战争故事和事情要告诉我们。我们

cues.en: have our corporate sponsor story. Exactly.
cues.zh: 有我们的企业赞助故事。正是如此。

cues.en: I mean, I have a lot of faith in the corporate world because it's always gonna be there, so you may as well have faith in it because if you don't, then that's just not good.
cues.zh: 我是说，我对企业界很有信心，因为它永远都会存在，所以你不妨对它抱有信心，因为如果你不这样，那可就不好了。

cues.zh: 加拿大最受欢迎的纪录片，
